blocks.text: Institut français de Tunisie — Tunis presents an exhibition by Michel Eisenlohr titled Images de Syrie: Palmyre, Alep, Damas , as part of the Jaou Tunis Festival , organized by the Kamel Lazaar Foundation .

A crossroads of civilizations, Syria has experienced painful and tragic events in recent years. Palmyra, a heritage of the shared past between East and West, is its martyred symbol. This previously unpublished reportage is a tribute to the beauty of this country and to the men who built, loved and protected it.

Invited to the Aleppo photography festival in 2002, Michel Eisenlohr decided to take to the road from Marseille. Like the writers who made their “journey to the Orient” in the 19th century, he approached this territory by road, kilometer after kilometer. For a travel notebook, a film camera and the deliberate choice of black and white.

In the middle of the desert, Palmyra is an essential stop. The grandeur and poetry of the ruins overwhelmed the photographer. The light leaves its mark there, chiseling the volume of the columns, cutting out the relief of the cornices. One believes the city abandoned to the wind; it turns out to be inhabited by shepherds who rest their flocks in the shade of its walls, and by children who find there an immense playground.

In Aleppo and Damascus, Michel Eisenlohr’s gaze was caught by the bustling life of the stalls, the floating fabrics, the dark cobbled alleys, and by an art of living that brings the different communities together in sharing and respect. The colonnades of the Roman city are answered by the arcades of the mosque, the ancient interlacing by the geometric patterns of Islamic art.
A dialogue of forms and societies. Such is the Syria the photographer discovered: sublime, generous, at times secret. A land of heritage living in the present.

Born in La Ciotat in 1974, Michel Eisenlohr has been an author-photographer for some twenty years. His photographic path is the fruit of a passion for travel literature, university studies on initiation rites, and of a taste for the other that he renews with each subject, each destination.

It was during a trip to the Dogon country in Mali in 1998 that he took his first images. Since then, he has continued his reportages abroad, around the Mediterranean, in West Africa, the Near East, India and, more recently, Iceland. He draws nourishment from encounters and cultures, in search of the Light that, laid on paper, reveals an image of the world. At the same time, he devotes himself to urban landscapes, the first theme being the city of his youth, Marseille, but also Genoa, Porto and Hong Kong and its urban enclaves, to which he has devoted an exhibition and a book. The spirit of cities but also the memory of places, such as the ruins of Palmyra in Syria, the former palaces of Menton and the fortifications perched along the Franco-Italian border. These are all subjects he looks at through personal reportages or institutional commissions.

With its many facets, Michel Eisenlohr’s work embodies great artistic freedom, drawing on the classical tradition of black-and-white photography, at times embracing pictorialist photography, and at other times mastering the most advanced digital techniques. His vision lies at the intersection of “pure” documentary photography and fine art photography. It is a photography of oxymorons, where opposites converge. A photographer who captures traces, light, and the intangible, his work is regularly exhibited in France and abroad and has been featured in several publications.

Exhibition Michel Eisenlohr: Images de Syrie: Palmyre, Alep, Damas October 27 to November 27, 2026 Institut français de Tunisie — Tunis 20-22, avenue de Paris 1002 Tunis https://www.institutfrancais-tunisie.com/list-agenda/#/
